scenes.title: Offset Management & Rebalancing
scenes.subtitle: Committing progress and reshuffling partitions safely
scenes.narration: Offset management records how far a consumer has read, while rebalancing redistributes partitions when group membership changes.

scenes.title: Committing Offsets
bullets: Auto-commit periodically saves offsets in the background
Manual commit gives precise control after processing
Committing too early risks data loss on a crash
scenes.narration: Auto-commit periodically saves offsets in the background at a fixed interval, which is convenient but imprecise. Manual commit lets you save offsets exactly after your processing succeeds, giving tighter control. Committing too early, before processing finishes, risks losing messages if the consumer crashes. Committing too late risks reprocessing already-handled messages, so timing is a deliberate trade-off.

scenes.title: What Happens During a Rebalance
scenes.narration: A rebalance begins when a consumer joins, leaves, or is deemed dead by the coordinator. The coordinator revokes current partition assignments across the group. It then reassigns partitions so every partition has exactly one owner again. Each consumer resumes from the last committed offset for its new partitions, which is why accurate commits matter so much.

scenes.title: Rebalance Strategies
scenes.narration: Older eager rebalancing revokes every partition from every consumer before reassigning, causing a brief stop-the-world pause for the whole group. Cooperative sticky rebalancing only revokes the partitions that actually need to move, so most consumers keep processing throughout. It is now the recommended default because it dramatically reduces disruption during scaling and deployments.

scenes.title: Manual Commit and Sticky Assignment
scenes.narration: This consumer disables auto-commit so it controls exactly when progress is recorded. It selects the cooperative-sticky assignment strategy to minimize rebalance disruption. In the loop it processes each message fully before committing the offset synchronously. This ordering delivers reliable at-least-once processing while keeping rebalances smooth.

scenes.text: Commit after processing, prefer cooperative-sticky rebalancing, and keep processing fast so a consumer is never mistaken for dead.
scenes.narration: As a best practice, commit after processing, prefer cooperative-sticky rebalancing, and keep your processing fast so a consumer is never mistakenly declared dead.
